questions.stem: In what exact ratio must rice costing Rs. 20 per kg be mathematically mixed with rice costing Rs. 30 per kg to obtain a mixture worth exactly Rs. 26 per kg?
questions.explanation: Using the rule of alligation: Quantity of cheaper / Quantity of dearer = (Price of dearer - Mean price) / (Mean price - Price of cheaper). Ratio = (30 - 26) / (26 - 20) = 4 / 6 = 2:3.

questions.stem: A specific mixture of 40 litres of milk and water currently contains 10% water. How many exact litres of pure water must be added to make it 20% water in the new mixture?
questions.explanation: Initial water = 10% of 40 = 4 litres. Let x litres of water be added. The new total volume is 40 + x. The new water content is 4 + x. We want (4 + x) to be 20% of (40 + x). (4 + x) / (40 + x) = 20/100 = 1/5. Cross-multiplying: 20 + 5x = 40 + x. 4x = 20, so x = 5 litres.

questions.stem: Two vessels A and B contain milk and water thoroughly mixed in the exact ratios of 4:3 and 2:3 respectively. In what strict ratio must these mixtures be mixed to form a new mixture containing exactly half milk and half water?
questions.explanation: Let's focus on the fraction of milk. Milk in A = 4/7. Milk in B = 2/5. Desired milk fraction = 1/2. Using alligation: Ratio = (1/2 - 2/5) : (4/7 - 1/2) = (5/10 - 4/10) : (8/14 - 7/14) = 1/10 : 1/14. Cross multiplying gives 14 : 10, which simplifies to 7:5.

questions.stem: A wholesale merchant has 1000 kg of sugar, a part of which he sells at exactly 8% profit and the rest at exactly 18% profit. He gains 14% on the whole transaction. What is the exact quantity sold at 18% profit?
questions.explanation: Using alligation on profits: Ratio of quantity at 8% to quantity at 18% = (18 - 14) / (14 - 8) = 4 / 6 = 2:3. Total parts = 2 + 3 = 5 parts. 5 parts = 1000 kg, so 1 part = 200 kg. Quantity sold at 18% profit is 3 parts = 3 × 200 = 600 kg.

questions.stem: A can contains a mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 7:5. When 9 litres of the mixture are drawn off and the can is filled with pure B, the ratio of A and B becomes 7:9. How many litres of liquid A was contained by the can initially?
questions.explanation: Let the total volume be V. After drawing 9L, the mixture volume is V-9. The fraction of A is 7/12, so A = (7/12)(V-9). After adding 9L of B, the total volume is back to V, and the new fraction of A is 7/(7+9) = 7/16. Since no A was added, the amount of A remains constant: (7/12)(V-9) = (7/16)V. Divide by 7: (V-9)/12 = V/16 => 16V - 144 = 12V => 4V = 144 => V = 36L. Initially, A = (7/12) × 36 = 21 litres.

questions.stem: A full container initially contains 40 litres of pure milk. From this, exactly 4 litres of milk is taken out and replaced by water. This exact process is completely repeated further two more times. How much pure milk is now contained by the container?
questions.explanation: The formula for the amount of substance left after n operations is: Final = Initial × (1 - Taken_Out/Volume)^n. Here, Initial = 40, Taken_Out = 4, Volume = 40, and n = 3 (1 initial + 2 further repeats). Final Milk = 40 × (1 - 4/40)³ = 40 × (1 - 1/10)³ = 40 × (9/10)³ = 40 × (729/1000) = 4 × 7.29 = 29.16 litres.

questions.stem: A solid alloy contains copper, zinc, and nickel exactly in the ratio 5:3:2. The exact quantity of pure nickel (in kilograms) that must be added to 100 kg of this alloy to have the new ratio exactly 5:3:3 is:
questions.explanation: In 100 kg of the 5:3:2 alloy, total parts = 10. So 1 part = 10 kg. Copper = 50 kg, Zinc = 30 kg, Nickel = 20 kg. We want the new ratio of Cu:Zn:Ni to be 5:3:3. Since Cu is 50 and Zn is 30, they already perfectly represent the '5:3' part of the ratio. The new '3' parts for Nickel means Nickel must be 3 × 10 = 30 kg. The amount of Nickel to add is 30 - 20 = 10 kg.
